  "title": "A-level Psychology Paper 1 Introductory topics in psychology — Practice Paper",
  "instructions": [

    {
      "id": "q1",
      "label": "Question 1",
      "prompt": "Which of the following best describes compliance as a type of conformity?\n\nA. Changing private beliefs as well as public behaviour\nB. Publicly conforming while privately maintaining original views\nC. Adopting the views of the majority because they are seen as an expert source\nD. Conforming because of uncertainty about how to behave",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "label": "Question 2",
      "prompt": "Outline the authoritarian personality as an explanation of obedience.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q3",
      "label": "Question 3",
      "prompt": "A school council is voting on whether to keep a long-standing uniform rule. Most students privately dislike the rule, but each assumes the others support it, so nobody speaks against it and the rule is retained.\n\nExplain which concept from social influence best accounts for the students' behaviour.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q4",
      "label": "Question 4",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into minority influence. In your answer you should refer to studies of the processes by which minorities change the views of majorities.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q5",
      "label": "Question 5",
      "prompt": "Which of the following is a feature of the multi-store model of memory?\n\nA. The sensory register has a very large capacity\nB. Rehearsal transfers information from long-term memory to short-term memory\nC. Short-term memory is encoded mainly semantically\nD. Long-term memory has a duration of about 30 seconds",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q6",
      "label": "Question 6",
      "prompt": "A student is revising for an exam. She reads her notes aloud, then answers practice questions without looking at the notes. When she later tries to recall the material in a different room, she finds it harder than when she practised in her usual study room.\n\nUsing your knowledge of forgetting, explain the student's difficulty in recalling the material.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q7",
      "label": "Question 7",
      "prompt": "A researcher showed participants a film of a car collision. Group A was asked, 'How fast were the cars going when they smashed into each other?' Group B was asked, 'How fast were the cars going when they contacted each other?' One week later, Group A was more likely to report seeing broken glass, although there was none in the film.\n\nExplain how the findings of this study support the idea that memory is affected by leading questions.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q8",
      "label": "Question 8",
      "prompt": "Discuss the working memory model. In your answer you should include evaluation of the model using evidence from research.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q9",
      "label": "Question 9",
      "prompt": "Which of the following best describes the role of the superego in attachment according to learning theory?\n\nA. It is formed through identification with the same-sex parent during the phallic stage\nB. It develops as a result of classical conditioning between caregiver and infant\nC. It is innate and biological\nD. It is the store of learned rules that produces conformity in social influence",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q10",
      "label": "Question 10",
      "prompt": "A nursery worker notices that one toddler becomes very distressed when his mother leaves, but when she returns he approaches her and then pushes her away, refusing comfort.\n\nIdentify the attachment type the toddler is most likely showing and outline one behaviour the nursery worker might observe that supports this classification.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q11",
      "label": "Question 11",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by maternal deprivation.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q12",
      "label": "Question 12",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into the influence of early attachment on adult relationships.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q13",
      "label": "Question 13",
      "prompt": "Which of the following approaches to psychology is most associated with the idea that people have free will and an innate drive towards personal growth?\n\nA. Psychodynamic\nB. Behaviourist\nC. Humanistic\nD. Cognitive",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q14",
      "label": "Question 14",
      "prompt": "A psychologist observes that a child who is praised for tidying her toys continues to tidy them, but when the praise stops the behaviour declines.\n\nOutline how the behaviourist approach would explain the child's behaviour.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q15",
      "label": "Question 15",
      "prompt": "Outline one limitation of using case studies of brain-damaged patients to support the working memory model.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q16",
      "label": "Question 16",
      "prompt": "Discuss the psychodynamic approach in psychology. In your answer you should include explanation of key concepts and evaluation of the approach as a whole.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q17",
      "label": "Question 17",
      "prompt": "Which of the following is a strength of the cognitive approach to explaining behaviour?\n\nA. It uses highly scientific experimental methods\nB. It explains all behaviour as the result of reinforcement\nC. It ignores internal mental processes\nD. It focuses only on observable behaviour",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q18",
      "label": "Question 18",
      "prompt": "A psychologist wants to investigate whether the presence of others improves performance on a simple task. She asks participants to complete a word-search either alone or in front of an audience. She then compares the mean number of words found in each condition.\n\nIdentify the experimental design used in this study and outline one advantage of this design.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q19",
      "label": "Question 19",
      "prompt": "Outline the role of the id, ego and superego in the psychodynamic explanation of behaviour.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q20",
      "label": "Question 20",
      "prompt": "A researcher is investigating whether there is a difference in the mean number of words recalled by participants who learn a word list in silence compared with those who learn it with background music. She calculates the mean and standard deviation for each condition.\n\nExplain how the standard deviation helps the researcher interpret the results of this study.",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q21",
      "label": "Question 21",
      "prompt": "Discuss one or more research studies relating to social-psychological factors in obedience. In your answer you should refer to research into the influence of authority figures and situational variables on obedience.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q22",
      "label": "AQA A-level Psychology Paper 1 — Practice Paper",
      "prompt": "AQA A-level Psychology Paper 1 — Practice Paper",
      "marks": 0,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q23",
      "label": "Question 23",
      "prompt": "Which of the following best describes the term 'schema' in the cognitive approach?\n\nA. A mental framework of beliefs and expectations that helps organise experience\nB. An innate drive towards self-actualisation\nC. A learned association between a stimulus and a response\nD. A conflict between the id and the superego",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q24",
      "label": "Question 24",
      "prompt": "A student who is anxious about exams finds it hard to concentrate in lessons. Her teacher suggests that the anxiety is caused not by the exams themselves but by the student's irrational beliefs about what will happen if she fails.\n\nOutline how the cognitive approach would explain the student's anxiety.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q25",
      "label": "Question 25",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by the term 'identification' in the context of social influence.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q26",
      "label": "Question 26",
      "prompt": "A psychologist carried out a study of conformity. Participants were shown a standard line and asked to judge which of three comparison lines was the same length. Confederates deliberately gave wrong answers on most trials. On critical trials, about one third of participants' responses agreed with the confederates' incorrect answers.\n\nExplain how the design of this study allows the researcher to measure conformity.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q27",
      " "  : "",
      "label": "Question 27",
      "prompt": "Outline the procedure and findings of one study of the capacity of short-term memory.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q28",
      "label": "Question 28",
    "prompt": "A researcher wants to investigate whether the type of attachment a child has with their caregiver is related to later friendship quality. She recruits 60 children aged 10–11 and classifies each child's attachment type using a standard interview. She then asks their teachers to rate friendship quality on a scale from 1 (very poor) to 10 (very good). The results are shown in the table below.\n\nMean friendship quality ratings by attachment type\n\nAttachment type | Number of children | Mean friendship quality rating\nSecure | 24 | 7.8\nInsecure-avoidant | 20 | 6.1\nInsecure-resistant | 16 | 5.4\n\nUsing the data in the table, explain what the results suggest about the relationship between attachment type and friendship quality.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": [
        {
          "id": "a1",
          "type": "table",
          "title": "Mean friendship quality ratings by attachment type",
          "content": "| Attachment type | Number of children | Mean friendship quality rating |\n|---|---|---|\n| Secure | 24 | 7.8 |\n| Insecure-avoidant | 20 | 6.1 |\n| Insecure-resistant | 16 | 5.4 |",
          "altText": "Table showing mean friendship quality ratings for three attachment types: secure (24 children, mean 7.8), insecure-avoidant (20 children, mean 6.1) and insecure-resistant (16 children, mean 5.4)."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "q29",
      "label": "Question 29",
      "prompt": "Outline the procedure of Ainsworth's Strange Situation.",
      "marks": 6,

      "role": "filler",
      "id": "q30",
      "label": "Question 30",
      "prompt": "Discuss the humanistic approach in psychology. In your answer you should include explanation of key concepts and evaluation of the approach.",
      "marks": 16,
      "assets": []

    "In extended 16-mark questions, candidates who plan a clear structure — description, application, evaluation — consistently score more highly than those who write everything they know about the topic.",
    "Application questions reward candidates who explicitly link scenario details to psychological concepts rather than writing generic textbook descriptions.",
    "In evaluation, candidates should aim for developed points: state the limitation or strength, explain why it matters, and where possible support it with research evidence.",
